name: JamSystem (network connection / JAM link pump)
summary: Owns the client's JAM network connection object (sys+0x28, name string 'JamSystem (%s)'). Each frame it updates a 1000-sample bandwidth/message-rate window, pumps the incoming-message queue, connects to a pending host:port, times out stale connections ('CheckConnections: Timing out...') and sends a periodic 250 ms keepalive/heartbeat message while connected.
tick: FUN_7ff650c462a0: rolling 1000-sample stats window (dt in ms). If not connected and a target address string exists (sys+0x3000) it resolves/connects (FUN_7ff650c45030, only when the global connection state at EA+0x170 +0xdc != 4). FUN_7ff650f02340(conn) = service the connection. FUN_7ff650c44e60 drains a critical-section-protected event queue (connect/disconnect events type 0/1). FUN_7ff650c45dc0: if link state (EA+0x170 +0x94)==3 and more than 5000 ms since last receive, logs '__CheckConnections: Timing out' and disconnects. FUN_7ff650c45b70: state 2 -> reconnect after 10 s; state 4 -> every 0.25 s builds a message and sends it through the EA's JAM handler at EA+0x1d0 (vtable+8).
callbacks: OnInitialize: sets conn+0x268=5 (flags), names the connection 'JamSystem (%s)', registers sys+0x30 as a listener on conn+0x20, calls conn vtable+0x10 (start). PreDelete tears the connection down.

key_functions.0x7ff650c45b70: reconnect / 250 ms heartbeat send via EA+0x1d0

server_relevance: Client transport only. A server needs the matching peer: accept the link, answer heartbeats and avoid the 5 s receive timeout.
evidence: Strings 'JamSystem (%s)' and '__CheckConnections: Timing out a...'; 5000/10000 ms timeouts; 0x3e800000 (0.25 s) resend timer; send through EA+0x1d0 vtable+8.

name: PathdataRebuildSystem (dynamic navmesh / pathdata tiles)
summary: Tracks dynamic obstacles (component 0x2a, and breakables 0x2d) and rebuilds the affected AI pathdata/navmesh tiles through a queue held in singleton component 0x64. An 8-state machine allocates big tile-build jobs (0x25f80-byte builders) and runs them async on the job system.
tick: Gets the map/pathdata object from EA vtable+0x70 (->+0x3a8 ->+0x158 pathdata, +0x168). Returns early if pathdata is missing or disabled. If a job is already running (0x64+0x340), it waits. Otherwise it runs a state machine on 0x64+0x2f0: state 0 (FUN_7ff650feae00) iterates component 0x2a. Each 0x2a instance compares its cached transform (from component 0x01) and movement-state bounds (component 0x12 +0xa050) against current values, throttled by a timer. On change it pushes the entity (with component 0x29) onto the dirty list at 0x64+0x328, then collects the dirty entries. State 1 (FUN_7ff650fecb40) pops a dirty tile coordinate (packed 12/12/8-bit xyz * cell size), allocates a 0x25f80 tile builder and schedules job FUN_7ff650fed070. States 2, 6 and 7 finalise or commit the tile (FUN_7ff650ed0f50 stores the new tile into pathdata+0x158).
callbacks: OnEntityAdded (entities with 0x29): pushes the 0x29 component's id into the 0x64 dirty list. OnEntityDeleting: if the entity has 0x29 with radius>0 (+0x30), adds its bounding sphere (+0x20..+0x30) to the 0x64 invalidation list at +0x2f8. If it has component 0x64 and the system flag is set, calls FUN_7ff650ff8ec0 (cleanup).

key_functions.0x7ff650feae00: state0: scan 0x2a obstacles for transform/bounds change and mark dirty
key_functions.0x7ff650fecb40: state1: build one dirty tile (alloc 0x25f80 builder, schedule job)

server_relevance: Server-side AI navigation. Needed only if the server runs bots or pathing; players do not need it.
evidence: Iterates 0x2a (EA+0xb0+0x3f0); singleton 0x64 (+0x960); per-cell quantised coordinates ((v&0xfff)-0x800)*cellSize; 0x25f80 builder; async jobs named 'Unknown'; STUIdlePathdataInvalidateComponent exists in the same id range (0x2b).

name: LocalPlayerInputSystem
summary: Samples raw keyboard/mouse/gamepad input into the local player's command component (0x2f) every frame: button bitmask, the current weapon/ability slot key, and quantised mouse-delta yaw/pitch. Registers cvar player_GenerateRandomMovement ('For local player generate movement...').
tick: For each component 0x2f: clears the per-frame input fields (+0x1474..+0x1494). Unless input is captured by UI (input manager DAT_7ff651886688+0x95a), it reads mouse deltas (FUN_7ff650cce3f0), maps keybind table entries to a slot index (FUN_7ff650c7e0e0), and gathers buttons (c7e580, c7e6f0). FUN_7ff650c7f320 converts view deltas into quantised shorts at +0x1484/+0x1486. The results are copied and ORed into the accumulated command fields (+0x1464..+0x146c).
server_relevance: Client-only input sampling. The server receives the resulting commands and never runs this.
evidence: Iterates EA+0xb0+0x468 (0x2f local player); strings 'player_GenerateRandomMovement', 'For local player generate moveme...'; key-binding table scan; float->short quantisation of view angles.

name: UnsynchronizedMoverSystem
summary: Evaluates time-driven, unreplicated movers (component 0x7d STUUnsynchronizedMoverComponent: scripted platforms and animated props) from the shared game clock and writes their transform. It overrides none of the standard slots. Its work runs in a secondary command-frame listener interface at sys+0x10 (vtable 0x15c1ed8) and in extra slot 14.
tick: No OnTick. Listener slot 0 (FUN_7ff650fef780) is called per command frame with the CF number when the game state (+0x24)==4. It iterates 0x7d, lazily initialises each mover (FUN_7ff650ff3230), then calls system slot 14 (FUN_7ff650c029a0). Slot 14 converts CF to time (FUN_7ff65100ea30), subtracts clock offsets from the EA timing object (EA+0x218), evaluates the mover path (FUN_7ff650ff32f0) and writes the position and rotation into the scene/transform component 0x01 (FUN_7ff6509e45c0). Listener slot 2 (FUN_7ff650c02920) does the same at render-time interpolated time (ms*16000 based).

key_functions.0x7ff650fef780: CF listener: iterate 0x7d per command frame
key_functions.0x7ff650c029a0: slot14: evaluate mover at CF time -> write 0x01
key_functions.0x7ff650ff32f0: evaluate mover path at time t

server_relevance: Deterministic from the clock. The server must run the same evaluation (or the same clock) for collision against moving platforms, but nothing is replicated.
evidence: Iterates EA+0xb0+3000 (=0x7d, STU name STUUnsynchronizedMoverComponent); secondary vtable at +0x10 installed in the game EA constructor; CF number passed; writes transform via FUN_7ff6509e45c0 on component 0x01.

name: StatescriptUpdateSystem
summary: Main per-frame Statescript driver. It advances every StatescriptSyncMgr (component 0x23) by dt in ms, then runs the pending script work of all components in parallel jobs. The local player's clock context is swapped in while it runs. It also performs a randomised code-page CRC integrity check (anti-tamper) and notifies the lobby EA.
tick: Picks the time context: if the EA is the game EA it uses the local player's clock (FUN_7ff650c3b860 -> +0x94) or the default, temporarily overriding the shared clock (+4) around the work. FUN_7ff650c0d700 has about a 3% chance per frame to CRC32 a random 4 KB code page (report code 0x37 on mismatch), then calls FUN_7ff650ce8590. That function iterates 0x23, calls the SyncMgr (+0xc0) vfunc +0x1c0 with round(dt*1000) for components flagged +0x419, and then (FUN_7ff650ce8680) collects components with pending work (+0x14c0 count>0) and runs them across worker threads (FUN_7ff650ce87d0). Afterwards it notifies the lobby EA (DAT_7ff651813e18 vfunc+0x80 ->+8, and +0x40 listener) with the CF or time, then does another random page CRC check (code 0x2b/0x1d).

key_functions.0x7ff650c0d700: random CRC page check + run update
key_functions.0x7ff650ce8590: advance each 0x23 SyncMgr by dt ms
key_functions.0x7ff650ce8680: parallel update of 0x23 components with pending work

server_relevance: Server-side game logic. The server must advance Statescript on the same timeline (the CF clock), because all abilities and gamemode logic run here.
evidence: Iterates EA+0xb0+0x348 (0x23 Statescript); vfunc +0x1c0 on SyncMgr at +0xc0 with dt*1000; +0x14c0 pending list; CRC32 (0xedb88320) over 0x1000-byte pages with rdtsc%100 sampling.

name: CombatFeedbackSystem (breakables + recent-hit tracking)
summary: The Prometheus name is 'CombatSystem', but the code is client-side combat presentation. It applies breakable-object state (component 0x2d part masks) to their models and spawns debris records. From the local player's damage history (0x2f) it marks recently-hit health components (0x28 +0x485) for hit feedback and outlines. Registers cvar combat_disableReticle.
tick: FUN_7ff65103f8b0: for queued breakables, pushes debris spawn points (bounds + transform) into singleton 0x7b. It then retries pending breakables (+0x80 list) via FUN_7ff650ca3b00, which applies the inverted broken-part mask (+0x98/+0x9c) to the model (component 0x04 +0xa0) and removes an entry once applied. FUN_7ff650c87200 reads the local player's (FUN_7ff650c3a0d0) 0x2f damage ring buffer (+0x15e0, 16-byte {entityId, time} entries, count +0x17f4). Entries newer than the current CF minus a window set flag +0x485 on the target's health component 0x28. Iterating all 0x28, if any flag changed it raises EA dirty flag 0x800000.
callbacks: OnInitialize: registers cvar combat_disableReticle and a component-change callback for 0x2d on EA+0x198 (FUN_7ff650c85750 -> reapply breakable state). OnEntityAdded: breakable entities are queued (+0x80). For entities with 0x2f, a pending entry keyed by entity id (+0x68 list) is applied via FUN_7ff650c86fb0. OnEntityRemoved FUN_7ff65103f6e0 cleans up.

key_functions.0x7ff650ca3b00: apply breakable part mask to model
key_functions.0x7ff650c87200: mark recently-damaged 0x28 from local player history

server_relevance: Mostly client presentation. The breakable state (0x2d masks) and damage history are server-authored data, but this system only visualises them.
evidence: Subscriptions 0x2f/0x2d/0x28; strings 'combat_disableReticle', 'disable the first person reticle'; bit 0x2d/0x2f/0x28 component lookups; singleton 0x7b (EA+0xb0+0xb88); health +0x485/+0x484 flag pair.

name: FirstPersonSystem
summary: Manages first-person versus third-person model visibility for STUFirstPersonComponent (0x22) owners. It registers the firstPerson_* debug cvars (model GUID, frame display, offsets, weapon-view offsets, detach flag, draw third-person model).
tick: FUN_7ff650c8d550 (update), then for each 0x22 with a first-person model entity (+0x20): if the owner is not the currently viewed entity (0x1f view backref check via FUN_7ff650c3e8e0), it hides render flags 0x200000000000|0x8000 on the FP model's scene component 0x01. Otherwise it queries the owner's component 0x23 Statescript var (FUN_7ff650f25a80/FUN_7ff65106b470) to decide whether to show the FP model, and sets or clears the same render flags on the owner.
callbacks: OnInitialize registers cvars firstPerson_ModelGuid, firstPerson_ShowFrameFlag, firstPerson_Offset{X,Y,Z,Yaw,Pitch,Roll}, firstPerson_WeaponviewOffset{X,Y,Z,Yaw,Pitch,Roll}, firstPerson_DetachModelFlag, firstPerson_DrawThirdPersonModel.
evidence: Iterates EA+0xb0+0x330 (0x22 STUFirstPersonComponent); many 'firstPerson_*' cvar strings; FUN_7ff6509c5c80/5b70 set/clear render flag bits.

name: LocalHitEffectsSystem
summary: Drives local hit feedback effects (reticle hit markers, screen-edge damage indicators, camera hit effects) from health-change events. Registers cvars localhiteffects_reticle, localhiteffects_edge and localhiteffects_camera.
tick: Random anti-tamper counter touch. For each component 0x33 it runs four updates: FUN_7ff650c928a0 and FUN_7ff650c92420 (with dt), then c926b0 and c927b0. Then a PEB NtGlobalFlag anti-debug check (report code 0x54).
callbacks: OnInitialize registers a component-change callback for health 0x28 on EA+0x198 (FUN_7ff650c90fb0 -> records hits/damage for effects) and the three localhiteffects_* cvars ('render reticle hit effects', 'render edge effects', 'render camera hit effects').
evidence: Strings 'localhiteffects_reticle/edge/camera', 'render reticle hit effects'; iterates EA+0xb0+0x4c8 (0x33); 0x28 change hook.

name: InstanceMessageDispatchSystem (JAM in-instance protocol router)
summary: JAM route table for the in-game (instance) protocols. OnInitialize registers handlers for 8 protocol groups keyed by protocol hash (0xe3c778bc -> ClientInInstance_Dispatch, 0x469a6c4d, 0x94f2c3db, 0xf9ad60eb, 0xdb201097, 0xf0877b67, ...). OnTick drains the thread-safe queue of received messages and dispatches each to its registered handlers on the main thread.
tick: Tail-calls FUN_7ff651031fb0(sys, sys+0x170): under the critical section at sys+0x180 it splices the incoming message list. For each message FUN_7ff651032390 looks up the protocol id (msg vtable+0x10 -> +0x18) in the route map at sys+0xb0 and calls every handler's vfunc +0x10(sys+0x1a8, msg), then releases the refcounts.
callbacks: OnInitialize FUN_7ff650c50790 runs 8 registration helpers on sys+0xb0. Each creates a handler object whose callback checks msg+0x48==0 and that the target instance id matches the EA's (EA+0x2a0 vfunc+0x20) before dispatching to the protocol's generated dispatcher (e.g. ClientInInstance_Dispatch).

key_functions.0x7ff651032390: route message to handlers by protocol id

server_relevance: Client receive path for all server->client game messages. A server must emit messages on these protocols (hash-keyed) with the matching instance id.
evidence: Registration helpers each use a distinct 32-bit protocol hash; handler callback calls the already-named ClientInInstance_Dispatch; critical-section-protected message list drained in OnTick.

name: PlayerNameCacheSystem
summary: When an entity with component 0x13 is added, it records that entity's 128-bit account/player id (+0xa0) and display-name string (+0x90) into an LRU name cache (max 1024 entries, with prefix/normalised-name indexes). The cache lives in the lobby EA's singleton component 0x65, so names persist across matches.
callbacks: OnEntityAdded(0x13): name = FUN_7ff6510324e0(comp) (string at +0x90), cache = FUN_7ff650c281a0() (lobby EA DAT_7ff651813e18 singleton 0x65, EA+0xb0+0x978). FUN_7ff650cb5690 inserts or refreshes the id->name entry. If the id equals the local account id (DAT_7ff65183a0b8/c0) it is stored in the self slot. Otherwise the LRU list is capped at 0x400 and index maps are built by normalised name and first characters.
server_relevance: Client UI or social only. The server just has to populate component 0x13 (id + name) for player entities.
evidence: Single subscription 0x13; 128-bit key compared against local account id globals; string copies; 0x3ff cap; lobby-EA singleton 0x978/0x18=0x65.

name: PlayTimeNotificationSystem (lobby session timers)
summary: Lobby-EA timer system that works on the account/session singleton returned by FUN_7ff650c24f80 (which holds the local account id at +0x60). While it is enabled (+0x18) it accumulates elapsed ms (+0x28), counts down a remaining-time value (+0x20), and fires up to two one-shot threshold notifications (+0x30/+0x48 entries) that format a value and display it through a UI string (GUID 0x0ac00000000005d5).
tick: The OnTick thunk jumps to FUN_7ff650c5cf70: dt->ms, updates the elapsed and remaining counters, and for each of 2 alert slots whose threshold has passed, formats the text (FUN_7ff650832ee0) and pushes it to UI element 0xac..5d5 (FUN_7ff650cc07e0/FUN_7ff650cc0e10).
server_relevance: Client or lobby UI only. The meaning of the thresholds is not confirmed (they could be play-time or queue/session warnings).
evidence: ms accumulator plus countdown and 2 alert slots with 'fired' byte; UI GUID 0x0ac00000000005d5; same singleton later updated by lobby JAM message 0x6d61.

name: AntiTamperHeartbeatSystem (lobby)
summary: A lobby system with no gameplay function. Its OnTick only runs the inlined anti-cheat/integrity stubs: an rdtsc-sampled touch of the page-CRC table, a PEB/ntdll ('ntdll.dll' built on the stack) check, and report code 0x56. These stubs are NOP-padded and short-circuited by JMPs in the treated binary.
tick: rdtsc%100<5 -> sync DAT_7ff6517fd478+0x34. Reads gs:[0x60] (PEB) and builds 'ntdll.dll' on the stack, but jumps past the checks.
evidence: Disassembly: NOP sleds, RDTSC mod 100, GS:[0x60] PEB reads, 'ntdl'/'l.dl' dwords, report code 0x56, and the same 0xffffffb9... stub bytes as other integrity checks.

name: LobbyJamHandlerContext (marker system)
summary: A 0x10-byte system with no overridden callbacks, cached at lobby EA+0x1f0. It serves as a type-identified context object: FUN_7ff650c486a0 finds it in an EA's system list via its type descriptor 0x7ff651798040. A JAM handler (FUN_7ff650c474a0 -> FUN_7ff650c48720) then uses it for lobby/account messages 0x6d60, 0x6d61 (updates the account singleton FUN_7ff650c24f80) and 0x6d62.

key_functions.0x7ff650c486a0: find this system in EA system list by type

evidence: All vtable slots are defaults; its only xref is the type check in FUN_7ff650c486a0, called from a JAM route callback.

name: LobbyFrontendStartupSystem (EntityStartup)
summary: EntityStartup-derived system in the lobby EA. It spawns the frontend/lobby entity from entity definition 0x4000000000001f1 (base slot 14 FUN_7ff650d14e10, which stores the entity id at +0x18), starts its Statescript graphs (0x58000000000041a/41b), and each frame pushes lobby/game state into that entity's Statescript dynamic variables. It also installs three input-binding resources (type 0x9a).
tick: If the lobby entity does not exist: spawns it (slot 14) and starts graphs 0x58..41a and 0x58..41b on its 0x23 component (vfunc +0x58). Then FUN_7ff650c7b520, b680, b740 and b8f0 set Statescript vars (ids 0x4d2, 0x8e3, 0x522, 0xa0d, 0x4aa, ...) from global state: game-EA mode==5, map GUID 0xd80000000000018, settings 0xd8..198/0xd8..984 and input focus. A var change raises EA dirty flag 0x4000. FUN_7ff650c7bc50 handles UI input. Key 0x9c toggles a debug global DAT_7ff65170615b.
callbacks: OnInitialize: loads 3 resources of type 0x9a (0x9a0000000000273, 0x...29b, 0x...29c) and registers them with the input manager (DAT_7ff651886688+0x10). PreDelete: destroys the spawned entity's scripts (slot 15), unloads the 3 resources.

key_functions.0x7ff650d14e10: EntityStartup base: spawn entity from def GUID

evidence: Slot 16 returns 0x4000000000001f1 (entity def); graph GUIDs of type 0x058; FUN_7ff65101b800 var sets with 0x40000|id; three 0x9a resources pushed to the input manager.
